name: l2c-of-hello
in:
# hello (23.8): a program of language 2 that prints "Hi" and a line break. A = 10 (the channels are at 3fb, 3fc), a layer has
# P = 4 slots of 4A = 40 bits. Labels count the bits from `o`, the start of space; they are defined before they are used,
# so layer 0 (the first thing in space) only jumps to layer 1 by a number. The rows of the channels are rows of language 1.
w a
# the boot packet: slot 0 copies the rest of the image (1c0 bits) over the snapshot, three slots are empty
r 0 1c0 3fb 3fb
z 78
# layer 0 at 0: the jump copies layer 1 (at d0 = 208) over the processor
r 0 a0 d0 170
z 78
# the data at a0 = 160: the buffer b; the bytes H, i and a line break (every bit of a byte in the order of the stream)
s 000000000000000000000000
s 01001000
s 01101001
s 00001010
# layer 1 at d0: three copies into the buffer, then the jump to layer 2 (at 170 = 368)
r a0 a8 b8 c0
r a8 b0 c0 c8
r b0 b8 c8 d0
r 0 a0 170 210
# layer 2 at 170: the buffer goes to stdout, then the jump copies a layer of NOPs (at 210 = 528): halt
r 3fc 3fc a0 b8
r 0 a0 210 2b0

name: l2l-of-hello_names
in:
# hello_names (23.9, part 1): the program hello.l2 with names of labels (tower/l2ltext.py) in place of one letter, and a reference
# forward: the jump of layer 0 names layer 1, which comes after it. The tool l2l reads this text twice (the first pass finds the
# labels) and gives the text of language 1 which l2c gives for hello.l2: the same image (A = 10, prints "Hi" and a line break).
w a
# the boot packet: slot 0 copies the rest of the image (1c0 bits) over the snapshot, three slots are empty
r 0 1c0 3fb 3fb
z 78
# layer 0 at 0: the jump copies layer 1 (a0 bits at d0) over the processor; layer 1 is defined below
r 0 a0 d0 170
z 78
# the data (a0 = 160): the buffer and the bytes H, i and a line break (every bit of a byte in the order of the stream)
s 000000000000000000000000
s 01001000
s 01101001
s 00001010
# layer 1: three copies into the buffer, then the jump to layer 2
r a0 a8 b8 c0
r a8 b0 c0 c8
r b0 b8 c8 d0
r 0 a0 170 210
# layer 2: the buffer goes to stdout, then the jump copies a layer of NOPs (50 bits after the end of the image): halt
r 3fc 3fc a0 b8
r 0 a0 210 2b0
